headlines.title: Alaric Jackson expected to miss two games after punching Chubb
headlines.summary: The NFL is expected to suspend Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson for two games without pay after he punched Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb following Monday night's 37–34 overtime loss, ESPN's sources reported. Yahoo Sports later reported the suspension as issued. Barring a successful appeal, Jackson would miss the Week 6 game against Arizona and the Week 7 game against the Raiders. The punch came as players gathered at midfield for the post-game handshakes.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Rams are 2–3 and ninth in the NFC, and they would lose their left tackle for the game against the Raiders.

headlines.title: Bears lose Montez Sweat for two games, activate Shemar Turner
headlines.summary: Bears defensive end Montez Sweat has been suspended for two games without pay for violating the NFL's performance-enhancing substances policy. He misses Week 6 at Atlanta and Week 7 against New England, and is eligible to return on Oct. 23. Sweat has seven tackles and two sacks in five games, after leading the Bears with 10 sacks last season. The Bears activated Shemar Turner off the PUP list to take Sweat's roster spot. Turner is a former second-round pick who tore an ACL in October 2025.
headlines.whyItMatters: Austin Booker leads the thin defensive end group with four sacks, and Turner gives the group some depth.

headlines.title: Rams release kicker Harrison Mevis and sign Blake Grupe
headlines.summary: The Rams are releasing kicker Harrison Mevis and signing Blake Grupe off the Jets' practice squad, sources told NFL Network. Mevis missed a 50-yard field goal in the first quarter and had a 48-yard attempt blocked in overtime, which would have won the game. Coach Sean McVay said the kicking was 'not even close to good enough'. Mevis was 5-for-9 on field goals this season. Grupe made 18 of 26 for the Saints last season and all 11 of his attempts with the Colts.
headlines.whyItMatters: ESPN Research says the Rams have had three blocked field goal attempts since the start of last season, tied for the most in the NFL.

headlines.title: NFL has until Oct. 20 to decide on a Week 8 flex change
headlines.summary: The NFL is considering a schedule change for the Sunday night flex slot in Week 8, CBS Sports reports. Philadelphia and Washington are both struggling, which is why the league is looking at it. Scheduling conflicts across the Week 8 slate leave few viable replacement games.
headlines.whyItMatters: The flex decision determines which game gets the Sunday night spot, and the options are limited.

teamNews.title: Cousins stays as the starter after Mendoza's late debut
teamNews.text: Klint Kubiak confirmed Kirk Cousins is still the starting quarterback, after Fernando Mendoza made his debut late in the 45–17 loss to New England. Athlon Sports wrote that the clock is ticking on Cousins, and Mendoza's first start is now a live question.

contextCard.title: How flex scheduling works
contextCard.body: In the later weeks of the season, the NFL can move a Sunday afternoon game into the Sunday night slot so the network gets a stronger matchup. The league has a set deadline to make these changes, which is why the Week 8 decision is due by Oct. 20. Flex changes are usually limited by which teams are free to play at night.

headlines.title: Giannis is eligible for an extension with Miami, and the timing matters
headlines.summary: Giannis Antetokounmpo became eligible for a contract extension with the Heat on Oct. 1. Milwaukee traded him to Miami on July 6. RealGM reports that holding off until January would add $82 million, and that waiting until the 2027 offseason would also allow him to sign for substantially more money.
headlines.whyItMatters: The money depends heavily on when he signs, and the gap RealGM describes is $82 million.

headlines.title: Celtics lock up Payton Pritchard on a two-year, $44.2 million deal
headlines.summary: Payton Pritchard has agreed to a two-year, $44.2 million extension with a mutual option for 2029–30, which ESPN reports is fully guaranteed. Yahoo Sports says it is the maximum extension Boston can give under the CBA. Pritchard averaged career highs of 17 points, 5.2 assists and 3.9 rebounds last season, starting 50 of his 79 games. He is the 2024 champion and 2025 Sixth Man of the Year, and he is likely to return to the bench this season.
headlines.whyItMatters: Boston is rebuilding around the players it kept after trading Jaylen Brown to Philadelphia, and Pritchard is now locked in through the mutual option.

headlines.title: Monday's extension deadline could bring a flurry of deals
headlines.summary: The deadline for rookie extensions is Monday, Oct. 19, the day before the regular season tips off. Five players have signed rookie extensions since the start of the offseason: Victor Wembanyama, Amen and Ausar Thompson, Keyonte George and Brandin Podziemski. ESPN's Bobby Marks says 17 of the 34 rookie extensions signed in the past three seasons came on deadline day. The same day is the deadline to extend veterans with two years left on their contracts, and to reduce rosters to 15 players on standard contracts. Karl-Anthony Towns has a player option decision, and Yahoo Sports expects him to turn it down, which would make him a free agent.
headlines.whyItMatters: Several teams will settle their contract plans on the same day, and Towns' decision would decide whether he hits the open market.

headlines.title: Kyrie Irving returns to the Mavericks with 17 points
headlines.summary: Kyrie Irving scored 17 points in his first game in 586 days, as Dallas beat Houston 132–115 in preseason. The Mavericks' offence looked more cohesive with him back. Irving has also praised teammate Cooper Flagg, comparing him to modern-day stars.
headlines.whyItMatters: Dallas looked more cohesive with Irving back, which matters as the Mavericks start the season with him in the lineup.
